functions.name: ScreenPointToRay
functions.doc: The ray from `camera` through `point`, in window pixels from the top-left of its target.

returns.doc: Whether there is a ray: false with no renderer, no such camera, or a point outside the camera's viewport.

parameters.name: ray
parameters.doc: The ray; the default ray when there is none.

functions.name: WorldToScreenPoint
functions.doc: Where `point`, in world space, appears on `camera`'s target, in window pixels from its top-left.

returns.doc: Whether it appears: false with no renderer, no such camera, or a point behind the camera.

parameters.name: screenPoint
parameters.doc: The point; zero when it does not appear.

functions.name: CameraAt
functions.doc: The camera drawn last at `point` of `window`, in window pixels from its top-left: the highest-order enabled camera in the active scene whose viewport holds it.

returns.doc: Whether there is one: false when there is none or no renderer.

parameters.name: camera
parameters.doc: The camera entity; no entity (the default Entity, C#'s Entity.None) when there is none.

functions.name: GetWorldBounds
functions.doc: The world-space box around the drawn meshes of `entity` and its children, now.

returns.doc: Whether there is one: false with no renderer, an entity not alive, or no mesh to bound (no MeshRenderer, or a mesh that does not resolve).

parameters.name: bounds
parameters.doc: The box; the default box when there is none.

functions.name: Stats
functions.doc: What the renderer did in the last drawn frame; zeros before the first.

returns.doc: Whether the app has a renderer.

parameters.name: stats
parameters.doc: The counts; zero with no renderer.

functions.name: SetSpotShadowBudget
functions.doc: Sets how many SpotLights may cast shadows from the next frame (RendererConfig::spotShadowBudget, ADR-0050): the nearest to any camera each frame; the rest light unshadowed. 0 shadows none.

returns.doc: Whether the app has a renderer.

functions.name: SetPointShadowBudget
functions.doc: Sets how many PointLights may cast shadows from the next frame (RendererConfig::pointShadowBudget, ADR-0050): the nearest to any camera each frame; the rest light unshadowed. 0 shadows none.

returns.doc: Whether the app has a renderer.

functions.name: SetGpuCulling
functions.doc: Turns the GPU frustum test (RendererConfig::gpuCulling, ADR-0057) on or off from the next frame, as Renderer::SetGpuCulling does: off, every cull pass keeps every candidate at level 0 and runs no occlusion phase, for comparison; the coarse cull of whole entities on the CPU stays on. Scripting never reaches RendererConfig, so this is C#'s way to the switch.

returns.doc: Whether the app has a renderer.

functions.name: SetOcclusionCulling
functions.doc: Turns occlusion culling (RendererConfig::occlusionCulling, ADR-0057) on or off from the next frame, as Renderer::SetOcclusionCulling does: off, each camera's cull pass runs once and keeps every copy inside its frustum, for comparison. Shadow views never cull by occlusion.

returns.doc: Whether the app has a renderer.

functions.name: SetCullingFrozen
functions.doc: Freezes culling from the next frame, or thaws it, as Renderer::SetCullingFrozen does (ADR-0057): frozen, each camera keeps the frustum and position it has in that frame and culls against them however it moves after, and the Debug stage draws each frozen frustum's edges, so flying out of it shows what was kept. Freezing while frozen keeps the first frame's volumes.

returns.doc: Whether the app has a renderer.

functions.name: SetLodSelection
functions.doc: Sets both level-of-detail thresholds from the next frame, as Renderer::SetLodSelection does (RendererConfig::lodErrorPixels and minProjectedPixels, ADR-0057): each copy of a mesh with levels draws at the coarsest level whose error, scaled by the copy's largest axis scale and projected at its distance from the camera, is under `lodErrorPixels` pixels, and a copy whose bounding sphere's radius projects under `minProjectedPixels` is dropped (0: never). Scripting never reaches RendererConfig, so this is C#'s way to both.

returns.doc: Whether the app has a renderer.

parameters.name: lodErrorPixels
parameters.doc: The error, in pixels, a drawn level may show; 1 by default.

parameters.name: minProjectedPixels
parameters.doc: The radius, in pixels, under which a copy is dropped; 0 by default.

functions.name: GetFrustum
functions.doc: The volume `camera` sees now (ADR-0057): the planes the renderer culls by, in world space from the camera's world matrix and its target's size, for a game that culls or streams its own entities. Five planes for a perspective camera, whose far plane is at infinity, six for an orthographic one.

returns.doc: Whether there is one: false with no renderer, no such camera, or a camera that draws nothing.

parameters.name: frustum
parameters.doc: The frustum; one with no planes, which everything is inside, when there is none.

functions.name: SpawnModel
functions.doc: Spawns `model` into the active scene as C++'s SpawnModel does, under `parent` unless it is no entity: a root named after the file holding one entity per node, each mesh a MeshRenderer, each skinned mesh with a SkinnedMesh naming its skeleton's owner, and with FenrirSkeleton installed a SkeletonPose on each owner and bone attachments below bones, given when the tree plays back. The root is usable at once (alive, so it can be given components or parented in the same call); the tree is made, as every structural change is, when the system returns. It needs no renderer in the app.

returns.doc: Whether it spawned: false when the app has no store, the model is stale or the parent is not alive.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.doc: The entity to spawn under; no entity (Entity.None in C#) for none. A parent that is not alive spawns nothing.

parameters.name: root
parameters.doc: The model's root entity; no entity (the default Entity, C#'s Entity.None) when nothing was spawned: an empty or stale model handle, no asset store, or a parent not alive.
